newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROY POSTS 37TH CAREER SHUTOUT AS AVALANCHE CRACK 100 POINTS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ROY POSTS 37TH CAREER SHUTOUT AS AVALANCHE CRACK 100 POINTS.

text.p: Patrick Roy faced 46 shots and stopped them all as the Colorado Avalanche blanked the Hartford Whalers 4-0 Tuesday to become the first team in the National Hockey League to crack 100 points.
Peter Forsberg and Valeri Kamensky each notched goal number 23 as Colorado improved to 46-19-9 for a league-leading 101 points.
Roy picked up his league-best 36th victory with his 37th career shutout. His seven shutouts this season tied him with Phoenix's Nikolai Khabibulin for the league lead.
Roy was especially sharp in the first period when he was tested 23 times, while the Avalanche scored twice on just eight shots on goal.

"They came out and played with a great deal of urgency," Colorado coach Marc Crwaford said of Hartford's first-period effort. "Patrick was just magnificent. That was the most chances we have ever given up in a period."
The Whalers outshot Colorado 46-28, but lost their sixth straight game.
Mike Ricci beat Sean Burke at 11:52 of the first period and Kamensky's powerplay goal with 67 seconds left in the period doubled the Colorado lead.
Adam Foote made it 3-0 3:37 into the middle period and the supremely talented Forsberg completed the scoring with an unassisted short-handed tally at 11:40 of the third.
"We got a pretty good indication of why they are the defending Stanley Cup Champions," Hartford coach Paul Maurice said.

At New Jersey, Vaclav Prospal and Mikael Renberg scored 84 seconds apart late in the third period as the Philadelphia Flyers edged the Devils 4-3 in a battle of the top two teams in the Eastern Conference.
Renberg's 21st goal with 3:24 left gave the Flyers a two-goal cushion, which proved crucial when Steve Thomas scored for the Devils a minute later.

Pat Faloon scored for the second successive game and John LeClair picked up his league-leading 48th goal in the first period as the Flyers opened a four-point lead over New Jersey atop the Eastern Confernce.
For the second straight game Philadelphia won without star centre Eric Lindros, who is nursing a bruised right calf.
At Tampa Bay, Rick Tabaracci stopped 28 shots and Alexander Selivanov and John Cullen each scored a goal and set up another as the Lightning blanked the Ottawa Senators 5-0.
Tabaracci was at his best in the first period when he turned aside 18 shots and helped the Lightning kill off three consecutive Ottawa power plays.
He faced just 10 more shots the rest of the way for his fifth shutout of the season and 12th of his career.
Paul Ysebaert, Patrick Poulin and Dino Ciccarelli also scored for the Lightning, who moved past Hartford into ninth place in the East, three points out of a playoff spot.
At Washington, defenceman Sergei Gonchar scored the tying and winning goals to lead the Capitals to a 3-2 victory over the St Louis Blues.

Gonchar, who missed the last 10 games with a knee sprain, knotted the game on an unassisted powerplay tally with 1:42 left in the second period. At 6:29 of the third, he poked his own rebound past goaltender Grant Fuhr for the game winner.
Brendan Witt also scored for Washington after Chris Pronger and Pierre Turgeon had given the Blues a 2-0 first-period lead.
In Calgary, Cory Stillman scored a goal and set up Sandy McCarthy's insurance tally, which turned out to be the game winner as the Flames edged the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 3-2.

Dave Gagner also scored and Jonas Hoglund set up two goals for the Flames, who moved into seventh place in the Western Conference playoff race, one point behind sixth-place Anaheim and one ahead of St Louis.
Paul Kariya, who notched his 38th goal, and Jari Kurri scored for the Ducks, who played without leading scorer Teemu Selanne, who suffered a strained oblique muscle Sunday.
